✍️ Exam Writing Guide

How to structure every answer by its marks — study this once, apply it everywhere.

This is the single writing-strategy reference for the whole question bank. The individual answers below contain only the exam-ready academic content; use this guide to decide how to present it on paper.

11-Mark Answers

Keep them crisp and direct — 1–2 lines (15–45 words).

  • Start with the key term or definition in the very first line.
  • Add one supporting fact, name or example and stop.
  • Never open with background or a full paragraph — the mark is for the point, not the story.

24-Mark Answers

A small structured answer, ¾–1 page (90–200 words).

  • Open with a one-line definition, then explain the concept briefly.
  • Add 3–4 points, each as point + explanation, not point only.
  • Include an example only if it directly helps; close with one summary line.

35-Mark Answers

A well-organised answer, 1–1½ pages (200–300 words).

  • Use headings: Definition → Explanation → Points/Features → Example → Conclusion.
  • Build basic → advanced: intro → definition → working → components → example → conclusion.
  • Programming questions need aim, steps, code, an important-line note and sample output.
  • Always close with a conclusion; a comparison table or diagram earns bonus clarity.

4Headings & Structure

Headings turn a block of text into a mark-friendly answer.

  • Use a heading for each distinct idea (Definition, Features, Example…).
  • Underline headings or number them (1. 2. 3.) — examiners tick what they can find.
  • Begin a new paragraph for each new point; keep one idea per point.

5Diagrams & Flow

A labelled diagram earns marks paragraphs cannot.

  • Draw for architecture, process, lifecycle, hierarchy or system design.
  • Keep it simple and label every box and arrow, then briefly explain it below.
  • For MongoDB/React/Angular, a small flow (e.g. Component → Virtual DOM → Real DOM) always fits.

6Presenting Code

Method marks come from the code, not from describing it.

  • Write aim → steps → program → explanation → output in order.
  • Comment key statements or explain them in the line below.
  • For queries, show the collection before and after the command.

7Keywords

Examiners scan for the syllabus vocabulary.

  • Use exact terms (BSON, Virtual DOM, $routeProvider) as they appear in the source.
  • Write each keyword in context once, in bold or underlined.
  • A keyword list alone is not an answer — every keyword must be attached to an explanation.

8Avoid Filler

Longer does not mean repetitive.

  • Never rewrite the same point in different words.
  • No openings like “In today’s world…” — go straight to the concept.
  • Increase length with new dimensions (features, working, examples, limitations), never with padding.
Golden rule: marks determine depth, the question type determines structure, the source determines terminology — and only academically relevant sections belong in the answer.

Q1

A ______ is defined as a record in MongoDB; MongoDB stores documents in ______.

A.Document, Collections
B.Application, Store
C.Table, Collections
D.None of the mentioned
✓ Correct Answer: A. Document, Collections
Explanation: A record in MongoDB is a document, and documents are stored in collections.
Q2

A document is a set of ______.

A.Key-value pairs
B.Application pairs
C.Activity pair set
D.None of the mentioned
✓ Correct Answer: A. Key-value pairs
Explanation: A MongoDB document is a set of key–value pairs (BSON).
Q3

Which field is always the first field in the document?

A._id
B.Ob_id
C.Id
D.Obid
✓ Correct Answer: A. _id
Explanation: _id is the unique primary key and is always the first field of a document.
Q4

In which format does MongoDB represent document structure?

A..txt
B..Docx
C.BSON
D.None of the mentioned
✓ Correct Answer: C. BSON
Explanation: MongoDB stores its document structure in BSON (Binary JSON) format.
Q5

In MongoDB, db.dropDatabase() is used for ______.

A.Creating Collection
B.Database Collection
C.Removing Database
D.None of the mentioned
✓ Correct Answer: C. Removing Database
Explanation: db.dropDatabase() drops/removes the current database.
Q6

Which is/are true about MongoDB?

A.Document oriented database
B.High performance database
C.MongoDB is cross-platform
D.All of the mentioned above
✓ Correct Answer: D. All of the mentioned above
Explanation: MongoDB is document-oriented, high-performance and cross-platform — All of the mentioned.
Q7

NoSQL databases are primarily designed to handle:

A.Relational data with fixed schema
B.Large Volume of unstructured and semi-structured data
C.Only transactional data
D.Only numerical data
✓ Correct Answer: B. Large Volume of unstructured and semi-structured data
Explanation: NoSQL databases are designed for large volumes of unstructured and semi-structured data.

Q19

What is a major advantage of NoSQL databases like MongoDB?

A.Fixed schema
B.Complex joins
C.High scalability and flexibility
D.Requires SQL syntax
✓ Correct Answer: C. High scalability and flexibility
Explanation: NoSQL databases trade rigid schemas for horizontal scalability and schema flexibility — documents with different fields can be stored side by side, and shards can be added to spread load.
Q20

Which of the following features is not typically associated with NoSQL databases?

A.Dynamic schema
B.High scalability
C.Complex joins
D.Distributed architecture
✓ Correct Answer: C. Complex joins
Explanation: NoSQL stores denormalised documents and deliberately avoids join. Complex joins are a relational (SQL) feature — in NoSQL you embed related data or reference it by _id instead.
Q21

Which command is used to create a new MongoDB database?

A.create db
B.use <db_name>
C.init db
D.db.create()
✓ Correct Answer: B. use <db_name>
Explanation: use <db_name> switches the shell to that database. MongoDB creates it lazily — it materialises on disk only when the first document is written. There is no CREATE DATABASE command.
Q22

What is the default behavior of MongoDB when a non-existent database is referenced with use?

A.It throws an error
B.It silently fails
C.It creates the database upon first write
D.It prompts for confirmation
✓ Correct Answer: C. It creates the database upon first write
Explanation: use never fails on an unknown name. MongoDB keeps the name as the current context and creates the database physically only when a document is first inserted into it.

Q32

Which of the following is NOT a valid MongoDB data type?

A.String
B.Integer
C.Float
D.Double
✓ Correct Answer: C. Float
Explanation: BSON defines String, Int/Long and Double — but not Float. MongoDB stores every non-integer number as a Double (IEEE 754, 64-bit).
Q33

In MongoDB, which data type would best represent a true/false value?

A.String
B.Boolean
C.Integer
D.Null
✓ Correct Answer: B. Boolean
Explanation: Boolean is a first-class BSON type holding true or false. Storing 0/1 as an integer works but loses the type, and Null only represents absence.
Q34

Which of the following is not a valid data type in MongoDB?

A.Binary
B.Double
C.Char
D.Object
✓ Correct Answer: C. Char
Explanation: Binary, Double and Object (embedded document) are all BSON types. There is no Char type — single characters are simply strings of length 1.

Q62

What does the db.collection.find() command do?

A.Deletes documents
B.Updates documents
C.Retrieves documents
D.Inserts documents
✓ Correct Answer: C. Retrieves documents
Explanation: find() is the read operation: it returns a cursor over the documents matching the filter, e.g. db.EMPL.find({ designation: "Manager" }).
Q63

Which MongoDB operator is used to check whether a value is present in an array?

A.$exists
B.$array
C.$in
D.$has
✓ Correct Answer: C. $in
Explanation: $in matches when the field value equals one of the listed values, which is how you test array membership: { tags: { $in: ["mongo"] } } matches any document whose tags array contains "mongo".
Q64

What does the db.collection.updateMany() method return?

A.List of all updated fields
B.Number of matched and modified documents
C.Cursor
D.Complete collection
✓ Correct Answer: B. Number of matched and modified documents
Explanation: updateMany() returns an UpdateResult carrying matchedCount, modifiedCount, upsertedCount and n. It does not return the documents or a cursor.
Q65

To remove all documents from a collection without dropping the collection itself:

A.db.collection.dropAll()
B.db.collection.clear()
C.db.collection.deleteMany({})
D.db.collection.removeAll()
✓ Correct Answer: C. db.collection.deleteMany({})
Explanation: deleteMany({}) passes an empty filter, so it matches every document and deletes them all while keeping the collection (and its indexes) in place. drop() would destroy the collection too.
Q66

Which of the following operators updates a field with a new value in MongoDB?

A.$set
B.$add
C.$put
D.$edit
✓ Correct Answer: A. $set
Explanation: $set assigns a value to a field, creating it if absent: { $set: { city: "Pune" } }. Use $inc to add to a number, $rename to rename and $unset to remove a field.

Q92

Which MongoDB operator is used to limit the number of results?

A.$limit
B.limit()
C.$slice
D.truncate()
✓ Correct Answer: B. limit()
Explanation: limit(n) is a cursor method that caps how many documents are returned — db.EMPL.find().limit(3). $limit is its aggregation-pipeline counterpart, and $slice only slices arrays.
Q93

Which operator is used to project only specific fields in MongoDB?

A.$match
B.$set
C.$project
D.$where
✓ Correct Answer: C. $project
Explanation: $project reshapes output — including a field makes it the only one returned, and a field prefixed with 0 is excluded: { name: 1, _id: 0 }.
Q94

Which MongoDB operation aggregates data from multiple documents?

A.db.find()
B.db.<collection>.aggregate()
C.db.concat()
D.db.group()
✓ Correct Answer: B. db.<collection>.aggregate()
Explanation: aggregate() is the collection-level method that runs a pipeline of stages ($match, $group, $sort, $project) and returns a cursor over the combined result. There is no db.aggregate() and no db.group().
Q95

Which of the following allows combining multiple aggregation stages in MongoDB?

A.db.aggregatePipeline()
B.db.collection.aggregate([])
C.db.pipeline.run()
D.db.collection.project()
✓ Correct Answer: B. db.collection.aggregate([])
Explanation: aggregate() accepts an array of stage documents and executes them in order, e.g. db.EMPL.aggregate([{ $match: {...} }, { $group: { _id: "$dept" } }]). Each stage consumes the output of the previous one.
Q96

Which statement is true about MongoDB's aggregation framework?

A.Aggregation cannot use indexes
B.$group must always follow $project
C.$match filters documents
D.Aggregation can't sort documents
✓ Correct Answer: C. $match filters documents
Explanation: $match filters documents at the start of a pipeline and can use an index when it is the first stage. Stages may be arranged in any order, and $sort is a normal stage, so A, B and D are all false.
Q97

Which of these commands sorts documents in ascending order by name?

A.db.users.find().sort({name: 1})
B.db.users.find().sort({name: "asc"})
C.db.users.find().orderBy({name: 1})
D.db.users.find().order({name: 1})
✓ Correct Answer: A. db.users.find().sort({name: 1})
Explanation: sort() takes 1 for ascending and -1 for descending; the strings "asc" and "desc" are not valid. orderBy() and order() are not MongoDB methods, and sort is a cursor method chained after find().
Q98

Which operator is used to retrieve documents that do not match a given condition?

A.$ne
B.$not
C.$exclude
D.$reject
✓ Correct Answer: B. $not
Explanation: $not negates the operator expression inside it: { price: { $not: { $gt: 100 } } } returns every document whose price is not greater than 100. $ne only performs a simple not-equal test on one field.

A.Props()
B.Properties()

Explanation: In a React class, properties are assigned inside the constructor() method.
Q127

The state of a component from inside a member function is accessed by ______.

A.this.getState()
B.this.value
C.this.prototype.stateValue
D.this.state

Explanation: Inside a member function, state is accessed with this.state.
Q128

A valid React component can return only ______ element.

A.2
B.3
C.1
D.4

Explanation: A valid React component must return exactly one parent element (wrap multiple in a fragment or div).
Q129

A valid React component accepts a single object argument with data and returns a React element. The object argument is ______.

A.Props
B.Function
C.Component
D.None of the above
✓ Correct Answer: A. Props
Explanation: A component receives data as a single object called props.
Q130

A state in React.js is also known as ______.

A.permanent storage
B.internal storage of the component
C.external storage of the component
D.all of the above
✓ Correct Answer: B. internal storage of the component
Explanation: State is the internal storage of the component — data it owns and can change.
Q131

To initiate a class, the ______ keyword is used.

A.Function
B.Class
C.ReactClass
D.ReactClassJs
✓ Correct Answer: B. Class
Explanation: A class is initiated (instantiated) with the class keyword / new.
Q132

Which method refers to the parent class?

A.Parent()
B.Super()
C.Top()
D.Main()
✓ Correct Answer: B. Super()
Explanation: super() refers to (calls) the parent class.
Q133

In React, ______ is used to pass data to a component from outside.

A.setState
B.Render with arguments
C.Props
D.PropTypes
✓ Correct Answer: C. Props
Explanation: Props are used to pass data into a component from outside (parent).
Q134

Which keyword is used for class inheritance?

A.Extends
B.Extend
C.Inheritance
D.Inheritances
✓ Correct Answer: A. Extends
Explanation: The extends keyword is used for class inheritance.
Q135

Which is the correct syntax of class inheritance?

A.class class1 extends class2{...}
B.class class1 extends class2{...}
C.class class1 extends class2{...}
D.class class1 extends class2{...}
✓ Correct Answer: A. class class1 extends class2{...}
Explanation: All four shown options are identical — the correct class-inheritance syntax is class class1 extends class2 { … }.
Q136★ Important

What are props in React?

DefinitionProps (short for properties) are read-only values passed from a parent to a child component to make it reusable and dynamic.
Example
Codefunction Welcome(props){ return <h1>Hello {props.name}</h1>; } <Welcome name="Rahul" /> // renders: Hello Rahul
•Props flow one-way — parent to child.
•They are read-only (immutable) — cannot be changed by the child.
•Make components reusable with different data.

What is the correct way to define a functional component in React?

A.function MyComponent() { return <div></div>; }
B.class MyComponent extends React.Component
C.new MyComponent()
D.component MyComponent()
✓ Correct Answer: A. function MyComponent() { return <div></div>; }
Explanation: A functional component is a plain function that returns JSX and is used as <MyComponent />. B is a class component, C instantiates wrongly (React does the calling) and D is not JavaScript syntax.
Q147

Which React hook is used to manage state in a functional component?

A.useContext
B.useEffect
C.useReducer
D.useState
✓ Correct Answer: D. useState
Explanation: useState(initial) returns [value, setValue] and is the primary state hook. useEffect handles side effects, useContext reads context and useReducer manages complex state via a reducer.
Q148

Which lifecycle hook in class components is used for side-effects like data fetch?

A.componentWillMount
B.componentDidMount
C.shouldComponentUpdate
D.render
✓ Correct Answer: B. componentDidMount
Explanation: componentDidMount() runs after the component is mounted, making it the correct place to fetch data or start timers. shouldComponentUpdate() is only a re-render guard, and render must stay side-effect free.
Q149

Which attribute is required to uniquely identify list elements in React?

A.id
B.name
C.key
D.index
✓ Correct Answer: C. key
Explanation: key is React's internal identifier used to track which item in a list changed. It is not rendered as an HTML attribute. Using the array index as the key is discouraged because it breaks when items are reordered.
Q150

Which is the correct use of useReducer?

A.useReducer(reducerFn, initialState)
B.useReducer(initialState)
C.useReducer({reducerFn, initialState})
D.useReducer(function, action)
✓ Correct Answer: A. useReducer(reducerFn, initialState)
Explanation: useReducer(reducer, initialState) takes the reducer function first, then the initial state, and returns [state, dispatch]. The action is supplied later to dispatch(action), never to the hook itself.

Q173

What is the use of useEffect hook in React?

A.Handling form input
B.Rendering UI
C.Performing side effects like API calls
D.Creating components
✓ Correct Answer: C. Performing side effects like API calls
Explanation: useEffect runs after render to perform side effects — API calls, subscriptions, timers, DOM measurement. It must not be used to derive state; useState handles values and JSX handles rendering.
Q174

What is the output of event.target.name in a form event?

A.The input value
B.The input ID
C.The input name attribute
D.The event type
✓ Correct Answer: C. The input name attribute
Explanation: event.target is the DOM element that fired the event, and .name returns its name attribute — not its value. event.target.value gives the value, which is why one handler can serve many named fields.
Q175

In React forms, which HTML element is used for a multi-line text input?

A.<input type="textarea">
B.<textarea>
C.<textbox>
D.<multiline>
✓ Correct Answer: B. <textarea>
Explanation: Multi-line input uses the <textarea> element with rows/cols. <input> is single-line only, and there is no textbox or multiline element — React has no built-in form components of its own.
Q176

Which hook is ideal for tracking a DOM reference in functional components?

A.useDOM
B.useRef
C.useMemo
D.useTarget
✓ Correct Answer: B. useRef
Explanation: useRef(initial) returns a mutable { current } box that persists across renders without causing one — ideal for holding a DOM node, a timer id or any mutable value.
Q177

How can React achieve conditional rendering inside JSX?

A.By using switch statements
B.Using if-else
C.Using ternary operators and logical &&
D.Using only external scripts
✓ Correct Answer: C. Using ternary operators and logical &&
Explanation: JSX accepts expressions, so {cond ? <A/> : <B/>} and {cond && <A/>} are the idiomatic forms. if-else and switch are statements and cannot be written directly inside {}.
Q178

Which hook is used to optimize a function so that it's not recreated on every render?

A.useMemo
B.useCallback
C.useState
D.useEffect
✓ Correct Answer: B. useCallback
Explanation: useCallback(fn, deps) memoises the function itself and returns the same reference until a dependency changes, so memoised children do not re-render. useMemo caches a computed *value* instead.
Q179

Which statement is true about useEffect?

A.It always runs only once
B.It runs after every render unless dependencies are specified
C.It replaces props
D.It prevents re-rendering
✓ Correct Answer: B. It runs after every render unless dependencies are specified
Explanation: With no dependency array the effect runs after every render. Passing [deps] limits it to runs where a dependency changed, and [] makes it run once on mount (the cleanup then runs on unmount).
Q180

Which component is used to create dropdowns in React forms?

A.<ListBox>
B.<DropList>
C.<select>
D.<Dropdown>
✓ Correct Answer: C. <select>
Explanation: A dropdown is the standard HTML <select> element containing <option> children. React supplies no <Dropdown> or <ListBox> component — ListBox, DropList and Dropdown are not real elements.
Q181

Which event handler is used for form submission in a React class component?

A.onChange
B.onSubmit
C.onClick
D.onInput
✓ Correct Answer: B. onSubmit
Explanation: React exposes the form's own onSubmit event; you call e.preventDefault() inside it to stop the page reload. handleSubmit is only a naming convention for your own method, not a React API.

Q240

Explain ngOnInit and ngOnChanges.

DefinitionngOnInit runs once after a component is created (used for initialization logic); ngOnChanges runs when an @Input() value changes.
ngOnInit
•Called once after the first ngOnChanges.
•Best place to load initial data / call services.
ngOnChanges
•Called whenever a bound @Input property changes.
•Receives a SimpleChanges object with previous and current values.
Example (Angular)
CodengOnInit() { this.loadData(); } // once ngOnChanges(c){ if(c.id) this.reload(); } // on input change

C.Both of the mentioned.

✓ Correct Answer: A. $dirty flag is used to state that the value has been changed.
Explanation: $dirty becomes true once the user has changed the input value (it does not indicate invalid data).

Q297

What Angular feature is used for making HTTP calls to REST APIs?

A.HttpRequest
B.WebClient
C.HttpClient
D.HttpFetch
✓ Correct Answer: C. HttpClient
Explanation: HttpClient is Angular's built-in HTTP client — it returns Observables and must be injected into a service or component. HttpRequest is a request model, while WebClient and HttpFetch are not Angular APIs.
